items.title: CVE-2026-113456
items.description:
visualTicket exposes sensitive information in error messages in the cinema report generator. An authenticated attacker with an admin privileges can supply an invalid date_from value causing the application to return a detailed error page that discloses the full SELECT statement (table and column names, JOIN, GROUP BY and ORDER BY clauses, bind parameter placeholders) and a PHP DateTime parsing exception.




This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

items.title: CVE-2026-113455
items.description:
visualTicket displays secret token value in admin settings panel. The "KSeF - Token API" edit form renders a pre-filled field containing the actual KSeF API integration secret without any masking.




This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

items.title: CVE-2026-113454
items.description:
visualTicket exposes sensitive information in error messages in the administrative report generator. Because application exception details and SQL queries are rendered in the HTTP response in the production environment, an authenticated administrator submitting an invalid date_from value in the report request receives a detailed error page disclosing the full SELECT statement, table and column names, JOINs, bind parameters, and a PHP DateTime exception.




This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

items.title: CVE-2026-113453
items.description:
visualTicket does not require authentication for the PDF invoice file serving functionality. Invoice PDF files reside in a web-accessible static path without a session check, while authorization is enforced only at the invoice registry page. A remote unauthenticated attacker who obtains the URL of an invoice PDF can download the document without authorization.




This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

items.title: CVE-2026-113452
items.description:
visualTicket is vulnerable to  Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the selectedDate parameter in the order summary page. An attacker can prepare a specially crafted URL that, when opened, results in arbitrary JavaScript execution in the victim's browser.




This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

items.title: CVE-2026-113451
items.description:
visualTicket is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) across multiple endpoints. State-changing operations are exposed via GET requests without any CSRF protection. A remote attacker can persuade an authenticated user (including administrator) into navigating to a prepared URL, causing the victim's browser to issue requests that carry the active session cookie and perform unintended actions.




This issue was partially addressed in version 20260817: settings changes and bulk refunds require POST with a CSRF token, and the session cookie is set with SameSite=Lax, which limits cross-site requests.

items.title: CVE-2026-113450
items.description:
visualTicket is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the JSONP callback parameter. An attacker can prepare a specially crafted URL that, when opened, results in arbitrary JavaScript execution in the victim's browser.




This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

items.title: CVE-2026-113449
items.description:
visualTicket is vulnerable to information exposure through JSONP on session-bound cart service endpoints. Session-bound data (including the session id, cart id, item ids, ticket/event metadata, quantities and prices) is returned inside a script wrapper, and since the symfony session token can also be passed in the URL, a remote attacker who obtains the token can read the cart session token and cart data.




This issue was mitigated in version 20260817: the session cookie is set with SameSite=Lax, which prevents other websites from reading cart data of the victim’s session.

items.title: CVE-2026-113448
items.description:
visualTicket is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting in logon functionality. An attacker can prepare a specially crafted URL that, when opened, results in arbitrary JavaScript execution in the victim's browser.




This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

items.title: CVE-2026-113447
items.description:
visualTicket is vulnerable to Session Fixation via the symfony session identifier passed in the URL. The application accepts the symfony session ID from the query string and set it as a session cookie in the HTTP response, allowing the browser's active session to be overwritten. This behaviour enables an attacker to fix a session ID for a victim and later hijack the authenticated session.




This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

items.title: CVE-2026-113446
items.description:
visualTicket is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the "culture" and "sf_culture" parameters. An attacker can prepare a specially crafted URL that, when opened, results in arbitrary JavaScript execution in the error page in the victim's browser.




This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

items.title: CVE-2026-113445
items.description:
visualTicket is vulnerable to information exposure through an error message in the order creation functionality. Because detailed data-layer exceptions are returned to the client instead of being logged server-side only, a remote unauthenticated attacker can submit a valid checkout request with an invalid payment_type value, causing the application to return a detailed SQL/ORM error that discloses the database name, table and column names, query structure, and foreign key constraint name.




This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

items.title: CVE-2026-113444
items.description:
visualTicket is vulnerable to Path Traversal in the thumbnail generation mechanism. The file parameter is used directly when constructing the output filesystem path without restriction to the uploads directory, allowing a remote attacker to use ../ sequences to escape /uploads/user_temp_images/ and write the generated JPEG file to other writable locations, including the web root. This allows unauthorized creation of JPEG files outside the intended uploads directory, leading to file-space pollution and potential overwriting of predictable resources with matching names.




This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

items.title: CVE-2026-113443
items.description:
visualTicket is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference  in the cart service. The server modifies or deletes a cart item based solely on the supplied "cart_id" without checking whether the object belongs to the current symfony session. Cart identifiers are created sequentially and allows prediction of valid values. An attacker holding an independent session can reference another user's "cart_id" and change its state, for example altering the quantity or deleting the item.  This allows modification or deletion of items in another user's cart, alteration of the cart total, and disruption of the reservation/purchase process.




This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

items.title: CVE-2026-111559
items.description:
Batflat CMS does not sanitize data passed to the /contact endpoint. A remote unauthenticated attacker can send a POST request with a crafted message, causing arbitrary PHP code execution with www-data user privileges.


The project is no longer maintained and the issue has not been fixed.

items.title: CVE-2026-129784
items.description: The httpx Ruby gem parses JSON response bodies through its transcoder layer. HTTPX::Response#json delegates to Transcoder::JSON.decode, and when the oj gem is loaded and multi_json is absent, the decoder falls back to json_load, which calls Oj.load(response.to_s) with no mode option. Oj.load defaults to :object mode, in which a response document can allocate any already-loaded Ruby class ("^o":"ClassName") and set its instance variables, or resolve a class or module reference ("^c":"Name"). An attacker who controls, or can influence, the URL an application fetches with HTTPX.get(url).json therefore controls object instantiation in the victim process. With a matching gadget chain, this issue can potentially cause remote code execution. Affects httpx 1.9.0; fixed in 1.9.1.

items.title: CVE-2026-99310

nfsd: hold cl_lock in client_has_openowners()

client_has_openowners() walks clp->cl_openowners and reads so_stateids
without clp->cl_lock. nfs4_put_stateowner() unhashes that openowner under
cl_lock and then frees it, so a concurrent EXCHANGE_ID with mismatched
creds can use-after-free the nfs4_openowner.

BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in client_has_state+0x10a/0x140
  fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c:3718 client_has_openowners()
  nfsd4_exchange_id
  nfsd4_proc_compound
  nfsd_dispatch
  svc_process

Take clp->cl_lock while client_has_openowners() walks the openowner
list.

items.description: A vulnerability has been identified in Rexroth IndraWorks. This flaw allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code on the user’s system by parsing a manipulated file, because the file parser fails to properly sanitize the path name(s) or references embedded in the manipulated file. items.description: The Burst Statistics WordPress plugin before 3.7.5 does not verify that a request is actually being routed to its own REST API before unloading every other active plugin for that request, allowing unauthenticated attackers to have requests processed with other plugins' protections (such as REST access restrictions, hidden login pages and two-factor authentication) switched off, and to cause other plugins' scheduled tasks to be discarded.

Attackers can post comments with img onerror payloads that execute when victims click Reply, stealing the non-HttpOnly sid session cookie to hijack accounts including administrators.

items.title: CVE-2026-129525
items.description: Several endpoints that work on both issues and pull requests did not check which of the two the addressed item is. A user who can read a repository's issues but not its pull requests could read pull request data through the issue sub-resources of the API (timeline, attachments, labels, subscriptions, tracked times and reactions), and list pull requests through the repository's issue search and milestone pages; the same applied in the other direction. The endpoint now only deletes attachments that the user uploaded and that are not yet linked to an issue, comment or release.

The token endpoint now refuses users who may not sign in, and token introspection reports their tokens as inactive.

items.title: CVE-2026-127958
items.description: A pull request review created through the API as a draft (`event` set to `PENDING` or left empty) was added to the pull request timeline and announced through notifications and activity feeds like a submitted review. Its body and line comments were therefore visible to everyone who can read the pull request, including anonymous visitors of a public repository, before the reviewer submitted it. Pending reviews no longer get a timeline entry or notifications until they are submitted.

items.title: CVE-2026-126338
items.description: Replying to a code review comment accepted a review ID that belongs to a different pull request, through the web form, the API and incoming mail replies. A signed-in user could reply on a pull request they can access with the ID of a review in a repository they cannot read, and the new comment was attached to that review and received the diff context of the commented lines. Replies are now only accepted for a review of the same pull request, and for a pending review only from its author.

items.title: CVE-2026-125617
items.description: `GET /api/v1/users/{username}/orgs/{org}/permissions` only checked that the organization is visible to the caller and then returned the named user's role in it. Any signed-in user could learn whether another user is an owner, admin or member of a public or limited organization, including for members who conceal their membership. The roles are now only returned to the user themselves, to members of the organization and to site administrators.

items.title: CVE-2026-123642
items.description: The AGit flow (pushing to `refs/for/...`) did not check the pusher's access to pull requests again when it created the pull request. A user or deploy key with read access to the code only, or with write access to the wiki over SSH, could open pull requests in a repository where they have no access to pull requests. Creating a pull request through AGit now requires read access to the pull requests of the repository and is refused for wiki pushes.

items.title: CVE-2026-123638
items.description: The "Protected file patterns" setting of a branch protection rule was checked against file names as git prints them, and git quotes names that contain a double quote, a backslash or a control character. Such names never matched a pattern, so a user with write access could add or change files under a protected pattern by direct push or through a pull request merge, and could move a protected file out of the pattern's reach by renaming it. Where the patterns protect workflow files, this allowed adding a workflow that then ran on the repository's runners. Changed files are now listed unquoted, and a rename reports both the old and the new path.

items.title: CVE-2026-123065
items.description: When a release was edited, the files of the attachments to remove were deleted by the identifiers submitted in the form rather than by the attachments verified to belong to the release. A user with write access to the releases of any repository, including their own, could submit a crafted identifier that resolves to the stored file of another attachment and delete it, provided they know that attachment's UUID. The attachment record stayed, so downloads of the affected issue, comment or release file failed. Release edits now only delete the files of attachments that belong to the release.

items.title: CVE-2026-123009
items.description: When a file is edited in a fork through the web editor, Gitea can first copy a branch from the base repository into the fork. That copy did not check whether the user may read the base repository's code. A user who had forked a repository and later lost access to it, for example after it was made private or they were removed as a collaborator, could keep copying its current branches into their fork and read them. The copy now requires read access to the code of the base repository.

items.title: CVE-2026-123002
items.description: Gitea accepted an unlimited number of wrong TOTP passcodes during sign-in, in the password reset flow and for Basic authentication with the `X-Gitea-OTP` header. An attacker who already knows an account's password could guess the six-digit passcode by trying codes at a high rate and sign in despite two-factor authentication. After five failed passcodes, further attempts for the account are now refused for 15 minutes.

items.title: CVE-2026-120991
items.description: When a container blob upload was rejected, for example because it exceeded a package size quota, the cleanup removed the blob from storage even if the same content already existed and was used by other packages. On an instance with a package quota configured, a user who can upload container images and has the exact content of another owner's package file or image layer could make it undownloadable. The cleanup now only removes blobs that the failed upload created.

items.title: CVE-2026-120729
items.description: The popup shown when hovering an issue reference loaded its data from the path of the hovered link and inserted part of the response as HTML. A user who can post a comment or other rendered content could add a link that is displayed as an ordinary issue reference but points to a file in a repository they control, so that the popup inserted that file's content into the page of anyone hovering the link and ran script in the viewer's session. The popup now requests the issue by the owner, repository and index parsed from the link.

items.title: CVE-2026-120725
items.description: With `REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW = true`, the Git LFS endpoints still answered unauthenticated requests for repositories that are not private. An anonymous client who knows the path of such a repository and the SHA-256 of an LFS object could download the object, and could use the batch endpoint to test whether an object exists. The Git LFS endpoints now require authentication when sign-in is required to view the instance.

items.title: CVE-2026-118535
items.description: A repository registered by its owner as a source of scoped workflows kept that registration when it was transferred to another owner. The new owner could then change the workflows in the transferred repository, and they kept running in the previous owner's repositories with access to their Actions secrets and job tokens. A transfer now removes the owner-level registrations of the repository, and registrations whose source repository no longer belongs to the registering owner are ignored.

items.title: CVE-2026-118389
items.description: The RubyGems package registry accepted gems whose platform, dependency names or dependency version requirements contain newline characters. Because the compact index served to clients is line-based, a user who can publish a gem to an owner's registry could forge index entries, such as packages that do not exist or additional versions of an existing gem with dependencies of their choice. Clients that resolve gems from that registry could then be led to install attacker-chosen dependencies. Gems with such metadata are now rejected.

items.title: CVE-2026-125423
items.description: A repository created with auto-init accepted pushes before its initialization had finished, and the initial commit was built in a checkout of whatever the repository already contained. A user who is allowed to create repositories could push a crafted tree during that window so that writing the README followed a symbolic link and overwrote a server-side git hook, which runs commands as the Gitea system user. The initial commit is now built in a freshly initialized directory, and a new repository only becomes ready, and accepts pushes, once its initialization is complete.

items.title: CVE-2026-123006
